data.description:
The proxy-usage-analysis skill's fast/cheap bucketing is wrong for windows spanning a mode transition.

## Problem

The analysis script (analyze_proxy_usage.py) derives the fast/cheap bucket split from the slot_schedule of the config profile for the mode active AT ANALYSIS TIME (config-fast.yaml / config-cheap.yaml per proxy/.mode). It never reconstructs the mode that was actually active DURING the analyzed window.

Observed failure (2026-08-12 window 01:00-11:47):
- The proxy ran CHEAP mode 01:00-10:00 (log evidence: 'Mode scheduler: applied scheduled mode cheap' at 01:00:20; status lines show total_slots=2 + contention_queue_policy=queue throughout 01:30-09:45) then FAST from 10:00 (applied at 10:00:29, total_slots=3 by 10:05).
- The report classified 153/153 sessions (100%) as Fast and 0 as Cheap, and showed 'slots: 3' for all sessions, because the analysis ran at 11:47 in fast mode and config-fast.yaml has a single 3-slot bucket (23:59->3, 10:00->3 -> equal counts collapse to one 'fast' bucket).

## Impact

- Fast/cheap split columns in report.md, fast_sessions.csv, cheap_sessions.csv are wrong for any window crossing 01:00/10:00 transitions (or a manual API mode switch).
- 'slots' column and per-slot context figures are wrong (report used 43691 = 131072/3; overnight the real per-slot context was 131072 = 262144/2 under cheap).
- Recommendations citing fast/cheap splits inherit the error.

## Evidence

Mode transitions are logged and parseable:
  'Mode scheduler: applied scheduled mode cheap' / '... fast'
  'Mode scheduler: enabled with 2 entries: ...'
Status lines expose the active profile: total_slots=<n> and contention_queue_policy=queue|fallback.

## Proposed fix (ACs)

1. The script parses 'Mode scheduler: applied scheduled mode <mode>' lines from proxy.log* to build a per-timestamp mode timeline covering the window.
2. Each session's fast/cheap bucket is keyed by the mode active at its first in-window stream time (falling back to current-mode config when no transition is observed in the window, e.g. single-mode windows).
3. Cheap sessions appear in cheap_sessions.csv; the report's Total/Fast/Cheap columns reflect the actual mode split (verified against a window spanning 01:00-11:00: ~9h cheap + 1h fast, not 100% fast).
4. 'slots' and per-slot context in CSV/report reflect the profile active for that session (2/262144 for cheap, 3/131072 for fast).
5. Existing tests pass; add a regression fixture using real 'Mode scheduler' + status_request lines.

## Notes

- Window-only reconstruction: sessions starting before the earliest observed transition in the window use the profile implied by the nearest prior transition in available logs (or analysis-time mode as today).
- Keep the existing behavior for windows entirely inside one mode (no transition observed): bucketing from the analysis-time config is correct there.
data.title: Proxy usage analysis: fast/cheap bucketing uses analysis-time config, not the mode active during the window

data.description:
# `wl delete` of a child reopens an in-progress parent

Discovered while running `/skill:plan LP-0MU148SHI004WHQM` (discovered-from:LP-0MU148SHI004WHQM).

## Problem

Deleting a child work item sets the parent's `status` to `open`, even when the
parent is `in-progress`. This silently breaks the claim invariant
**SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9** ("actively worked => `in_progress`"): an agent that
claims an item, creates/deletes a child, then continues mutating is now
performing work-item mutations while `status: open` — the exact window that
caused the 2026-08-30 duplicate dispatch of `AH-0MTFPDK006QUDC`.

`wl delete <child>` is documented as "marks as deleted", not as touching the
parent, so the parent reversion is unexpected.

## Reproduction (2026-09-26, Worklog via ContextHub)

```bash
# low-priority throwaway parent + child
P=$(wl create --title "__diag_parent__" --stage intake_complete --json | jq -r .workItem.id)
C=$(wl create --title "__diag_child__" --parent "$P" --stage intake_complete --json | jq -r .workItem.id)
wl update "$P" --status in_progress --json >/dev/null
wl show "$P" --json | jq -r .workItem.status   # in-progress
wl delete "$C" --json >/dev/null
wl show "$P" --json | jq -r .workItem.status   # open   <-- unexpected
```

Confirmed on 2026-09-26. `wl update --effort/--risk`, `wl create --parent`,
and `wl dep add` do **not** reproduce it; only child deletion does.

## Expected

Deleting a child must leave the parent's `status`/`stage` untouched (the parent
may legitimately stay `in-progress`; a deleted child does not make the subtree
"finished"). If a reversion is intended for some terminal-parent case, it must
require the parent to be `completed`/`in_review` (as
`demoteParentOnChildAdded` does) and never touch `in-progress`.

## Impact

- Breaks the claim invariant for any skill that deletes children mid-run.
- An item can silently drop out of `wl next`'s in-progress view mid-session.
- Background/downtime dispatchers may re-dispatch an item already being worked.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Reproducing the steps above leaves the parent `in-progress`/`intake_complete`.
- A regression test in the Worklog/ContextHub suite covers child deletion not
  changing a non-terminal parent's status or stage.
- The fix does not reintroduce the terminal-parent demotion behaviour described
  in `demoteParentOnChildAdded` (completed/`in_review` parents still reopen on
  gaining a new child).

## Notes

- Owner/component: Worklog CLI (`ContextHub`) — `wl delete` /
  `packages/shared/src/database.ts`.
- The original `LP-0MU148SHI004WHQM` plan run also showed the parent at
  `open` mid-run without any child deletion; that occurrence is not explained
  by this reproduction and may be a separate sync/concurrency effect, so it is
  not claimed as part of this bug.
data.title: wl delete of a child reopens an in-progress parent (claim invariant)

## Intake: open questions (needs producer input)

Investigation of the 2026-09-26 proxy-usage report recommendation
`### [HIGH] Stream finish errors: adopt recovery-first + informative-error strategy`
(window 2026-09-25 05:00 → 2026-09-26 05:00).

### Context gathered

Both recommended proxy-side strategies are **already implemented and shipped**:

- **Recovery-first re-route** — `_preflight_streaming_response()` in `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
  pre-consumes the stream and raises `StreamingPreContentError` so the fallback chain re-routes
  before content (LP-0MSETOTWY000SU0Z).
- **Informative error** — every synthetic `finish_reason: error` is built by
  `_build_stream_error_event()` (`proxy/proxy/proxy_remote.py`, also used by the local path in
  `proxy/proxy/router.py`); today's report confirms **31/31 residual events carry the enriched
  payload** (type/message/suggested-action).
- **Bounded mode-switch drain** — `proxy/proxy/mode.py` (LP-0MT631JKW008WAKE / LP-0MT60S55M000TK1H).

### Residual gap analysis — the 31 `stream_finish_error` events

| Count | Provider/model | Error | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| 24 | `opencode-go` / `deepseek-v4.1-flash` | `stall_after_content` | Upstream idle timeout after content delivered — the proxy cannot re-route after content; informative error is the correct terminal outcome. |
| 6 | `local` / `Qwen3` | `stream_exception` (`RemoteProtocolError`) | Log correlation: killed by mode-switch / llama-server restarts (17:27:58 restart → 2 killed at 17:28:00; 14:10:19 restart → 1 killed; 10:00 scheduled switch → 3 killed). The drain defers **new** requests but still kills **in-flight** local streams. |
| 1 | `deepseek` / `deepseek-flash` | `stream_exception` | Remote stream exception. |

**Client-visibility gap (material):** pi-ai maps `finish_reason: "error"` to the generic string
`Provider finish_reason: error` (`@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/providers/openai-completions.js`,
`mapStopReason`) — the enriched `type`/`message`/`suggested_action` is discarded **before the
client sees it**. ContextHub's recovery module
(`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts`) has no pattern matching that
string, so it falls through to `ErrorCategory.UNKNOWN` and is **not retried**. The informative
error therefore does not reach the client in an actionable form — contradicting the report's
"No client-side change required".

**Report-logic gap:** the `[HIGH]` recommendation title/text still says "adopt
recovery-first + informative-error strategy" even though the code and the report's own evidence
show both are adopted. `_error_recommendations()` in
`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/recommendations.py` fires whenever
`stream_finish_error > 0`, with no root-cause split.

### Q1 — Primary scope / deliverable

Which deliverable do you want from this work item?

- **(a)** Cross-repo epic: (i) make the report recommendation evidence-consistent and
  root-cause-classify residual events, (ii) add client-side recovery in ContextHub for the proxy
  stream error, (iii) fix the residual mode-switch restart kills and document
  `stall_after_content` as by-design. Children raised in both worklogs.
- **(b)** Report/analysis only — fix the stale HIGH recommendation and root-cause split.
- **(c)** Client only — make ContextHub's recovery extension interpret/retry the proxy stream error.
- **(d)** Proxy only — fix the residual restart kills; document the remote stalls as expected.

**Recommended:** (a) — the report now contradicts its own evidence, the client provably cannot see
the informative payload, and the drain fix is not holding; all three are linked, real gaps that
this single recommendation covers.

### Q2 — Client-side behaviour (if Q1 includes the client)

Given pi-ai drops the enriched payload (client only sees `Provider finish_reason: error`), how
should the client be fixed?

- **(a)** Add a retryable pattern for `finish_reason: error` / `Provider finish_reason: error` to
  ContextHub's `error-patterns.ts` (retry with backoff, as with the existing
  `"Stream ended without finish_reason"` case), and raise a separate upstream issue against pi-ai
  to forward the enriched `type`/`message`/`suggested_action`.
- **(b)** Patch/vendor pi-ai in ContextHub to forward the enriched payload, then classify on those
  fields (and surface `suggested_action`).
- **(c)** Other (please specify).

**Recommended:** (a) — minimal, fully in-repo, restores automatic retry immediately, and keeps the
upstream pi-ai change as a separately tracked issue.

### Q3 — ContextHub tracking

Should the client-side change be tracked as a **child work item in the ContextHub worklog**
(prefix `WL`) linked back to this LP item, or kept as an LP child that merely references the
ContextHub files?

**Recommended:** create it in the ContextHub `WL` store and link it — the change ships in that
repository, so it should be tracked where the code lives.

_Open questions recorded during intake; the intake brief will be finalised once these are
answered._
